title: Aughra · the eye of the world
opening: God made all things and in this way is all things.
framing: Opening statement supplied by the app’s author · spiritual reflection through The Dark Crystal

chapters.title: The world finding an eye
chapters.story: Aughra embodies Thra and carries its voice. Her removable eye makes perception a central image: the world becomes something that can be witnessed and answered.
chapters.human: Human parallel: attention carries responsibility. To see a hungry animal, a frightened child or a damaged landscape is to encounter a claim on our conduct. Your opening statement provides the spiritual frame: creation is cherished as belonging to God. Empathy turns another being from scenery into a neighbour.

chapters.title: Roots, rock and awakening
chapters.story: The official chronology places her emergence among rocks and trees before the later divisions of Thra. She shares practical knowledge with the Gelfling.
chapters.human: The lesson reads the eye, roots and stone as an image of embodied awareness. Human understanding grows through sensation, relationship and learning. Wonder and useful knowledge belong together: a beautiful vision should also help someone live, eat, find shelter or protect another being.

chapters.title: The observatory and the near world
chapters.story: The urSkeks share astronomical knowledge with Aughra; TekTih builds her observatory and orrery. Her attention reaches toward the cosmos.
chapters.human: There is a fruitful tension between looking outward and attending nearby. Scientific ambition, spiritual aspiration and technical invention can enlarge our understanding. Their ethical test includes what happens to the beings beside us. The telescope and the helping hand should remain connected.

chapters.title: The Great Division
chapters.story: The urSkeks attempt purification through the Crystal and emerge as Skeksis and Mystics. Their separated lives remain connected.
chapters.human: A human comparison is the division between capability and conscience: power cut off from empathy, or contemplation cut off from responsibility. The story offers a dramatic restoration of relationship. Its ending need not mean approving cruelty; a human reading can seek wholeness while rejecting abusive conduct and repairing its consequences.

chapters.title: Awakening to harm · Age of Resistance
chapters.story: In the prequel era, Aughra turns from distant study to the Gelfling struggle after recognising damage to the Crystal.
chapters.human: Awakening involves revising where attention goes. Prestige, an impressive institution or a beautiful promise does not settle whether an action helps. Listen to people affected, examine extraction and coercion, and distinguish a claim of benevolence from provision that actually reaches someone. This is a natural place for the app’s four-way assessment.

chapters.title: Jen and the shard
chapters.story: Jen is sent to Aughra. She offers the shards but cannot choose the right one for him. Garthim destroy the observatory and carry her away.
chapters.human: A teacher provides orientation without replacing the learner’s discernment. Knowledge becomes practical when someone chooses, acts and checks what follows. Threats to places of learning also threaten collective memory; preserving knowledge and making it accessible is a form of stewardship.

chapters.title: Kira and the creatures
chapters.story: Imprisoned, Aughra urges Kira to call on the captive creatures. Their response helps free them. Jen later restores the Crystal; the separated beings reunite.
chapters.human: The creatures are participants rather than expendable background. Human kinship with animals asks for patience, respect for their needs and protection from exploitation. Courage can be relational: people and other living beings can support one another. The lesson’s goal is release from harm, not domination.

chapters.title: The eye of the world · a human practice
chapters.story: Aughra’s arc moves between witnessing, learning, absence, return and assistance. The Crystal’s healing closes the film’s central rupture.
chapters.human: Practise the sequence: notice a being; listen before judging; identify a concrete need; choose a proportionate helpful act; check its effects; repair mistakes. Hold wonder together with accountability. In the app’s spiritual vocabulary, choose life and love the lamb in both light and dark. Darkness in a scene is not itself a verdict on the beings within it.
